BOOK: "How to Win Friends and Influence People" by Dale Carnegie
CHAPTER 17: "A Formula That Will Work Wonders for You"
EXAMPLE: "Yael and Ada at the Project Planning Table"
TONE: competitive (edge-seeking, strategic, advantage-focused)
CATEGORY: work

CURRENT SCENARIO (lacks quoted dialogue):
Yael has pitched a campaign timeline twice. Ada killed it twice. Yael stops selling and starts diagnosing. They sit at the break room table, coffee machine gurgling behind them.

Yael: 'You have pushed back twice. Help me understand the specific problem.'
Ada: 'It overlaps with the product launch prep. I am already behind on launch assets.'
Yael: 'So the campaign is not the problem. The collision is.'
Ada: 'Exactly. Two weeks later and I could do both. Right now, one gets my worst work, and I will not let that be the launch.'
Yael: 'What if we shift ten days and I handle the first round of campaign copy?'
Ada: [quiet for a moment] 'That works. I was not blocking you. I was trying not to deliver substandard work on either front.'

RULES:
- Rewrite to include at least 3 back-and-forth quoted speech exchanges using "double quotes"
- Keep the same characters, setting, and lesson
- Total length: 80-150 words
- Include 3+ concrete details (names, times, objects, locations) and 1 sensory/emotional detail
- Do NOT use em dashes (—) or double hyphens (--)
- Do NOT use banned phrases: delve, crucial, landscape, realm, furthermore, moreover
- Maintain the competitive tone
- Return ONLY the rewritten scenario text, no commentary

CHAPTER 18: "What Everybody Wants"
EXAMPLE: "How Etta Gained an Ally"
TONE: gentle (warm, reflective, sit-with-it framing)
CATEGORY: school

CURRENT SCENARIO (lacks quoted dialogue):
Etta notices that Ishan, a member of the environmental club, stopped coming after his cleanup proposal was voted down. She finds him in the hallway and says, 'If I had pitched an idea I really cared about and the group just moved on, I would feel like my effort did not count. Is that what happened?' What do you think happens next?

What unfolded: Ishan says, 'Nobody even acknowledged it was a good idea.' Rain taps the hallway window. Etta says, 'It was a good idea, and I should have said so.' Ishan returns to the next meeting and participates in the campaign he originally opposed. The vote never changed. What changed was his feeling of being dismissed.
